commits.message: Merge 05847c2771f272327731837257df491d0ca4f792 into 187446e996c21fe2bc395c27b0adcbeca49eafec

effects-playground: the terminal plays every effect at once, stacked as the demo's screen is (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

The kit's stage plays each program as a named scene on its own clock, one under another; replay and restart name their scene. npm run effects-playground:terminal follows every effect unless some are named; the server address is --server=.

effects-playground: play an effect in a real terminal beside the page, following every change (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

npm run effects-playground:terminal -- <effect> runs the panel's program in the terminal on the library the dev server builds; the page tells the server each edit, control, replay and restart over vite's socket, and the server relays them as server-sent events, state first. The kit gains an in-place restart.

effects-playground: show every colour as drawn; the docs' contrast floor is now a LiveTerminal option (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

xterm's minimumContrastRatio 4.5 redrew any cell faded toward its ground as readable text, so fade and dissolve never showed: words and powerline glyphs stayed visible while hidden. The docs' terminals keep READABLE_CONTRAST; the playground asks for 1.
effects-playground: magnitude slider to 100 (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

effects-playground: edits and run controls change the running program in place; live frames reach xterm whole (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

An edit is typed at the running program and run in its process; the kit's play swaps its scene in a mobx box, and controls (fps, rate, magnitude, theme, depth) and replay reach it the same way, so the clock and screen carry on. LiveTerminal holds DEC 2026 synchronized-output frames and writes each whole: xterm 5.3 ignores the mode and painted half-arrived frames, the flicker under slider drags. magnified() is the demo's per-curve magnitude rule, shared with the kit.

example-runner: a bundle's modules are files, not rolldown's made-up \0 ids; the playground's base64 workaround goes (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

addWatchFile on \0rolldown/runtime.js made vite fail resolving it as an import of the watching module on a fresh dev server.

effects-playground: each effect's code from curves.ts in an editor, sliders over its values, run in the docs' live terminal (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

A program is the effect's function as curves.ts has it and every
declaration it reaches, cut out at serve time (programs.ts), so the code
shown is the code the demo runs. Sliders are views of literals in that
text (tunables.ts); a slider edits the program and every run starts from
an edit. Programs import effects-kit, the demo's subjects and pacing,
added to the live library by libraryModule (example-runner.ts).
graphemes joins the main barrel so app.ts bundles onto the live library.
The runDemo effect subset and shapes the old page needed are gone.
effects-playground: its own vite config, answering on every interface to any host name (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

effects-playground: one page, one real terminal per effect running runDemo; defaults restored to the demo's (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Each playground mounts runDemo on BrowserTerminalHost over xterm, showing
one effect (Settings.effects), so renderer, pacing and keys are the demo's.
Transition shapes travel on Settings.shapes. DISSOLVE_SHAPE, the dissolve
duration and the rebound test are back to their pre-playground values.
effects-playground: font controls (WIP; playground rejected, to be rebuilt on the docs terminal) (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)
effects-feel: a browser playground, one panel per effect with every constant adjustable; dissolve's rebound made large enough to see (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)
effects-feel: the frame counter counts frames since the cycle began, across rate changes (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)
effects-feel: one sync block around a printed line's erase, text and repaint; a same-rate set keeps the timer; wheel stray is not eased; fps steps reach off-grid neighbours (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

effects-feel: keep shimmer, sparkle, wheel, fade, dissolve; pulse chosen elements gently; dissolve eddies back; drop drift (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Brandon approved shimmer, sparkle, wheel, fade and dissolve. Drift and the
sleeper's-breath pulse are gone. Pulse is now a gentle glow on chosen UI
elements (the strip's 'ctx 61%' and 'ok' cells), each at a time of its own,
the rest of the screen untouched. Dissolve now lets patches of what is left
rise back part way near the end before thinning away.
effects-feel: the wheel turns a powerline cap with the cell it caps (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

effects-feel: a hue wheel, every segment at its own pace; prime periods; time runs on across cycles (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

A fifth loop: every hue turning the whole way round once a period, 907
designed seconds — too slow to see moving, plain after an hour away.
Each segment (a colour of the element's own) strays from the shared turn
on slow noise of its own at 211 and 337 seconds; the swing is how far,
1 being half a turn apart. Lightness and chroma are kept.

Every loop's default period is prime (109, 43, 79, 139, 907), so no two
come back into step within a sitting. Demo time no longer winds back at
a cycle, since that would jump a wheel mid-turn: it runs on, cycles are
counted, and only the transitions replay at each.

effects-feel: [ and ] scale every loop's swing (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

A magnitude, ×1 the flags' swings, a quarter a press from ×0.25 to ×4; a
mix toward a light stops at the light, drift's degrees do not. The scene is
rebuilt at the new swings, its contrast measured again between the frames.

effects-feel: a frame is the unit of change, whatever the frame rate (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

The app runs on a clock that counts frames, so each tick moves every loop
by one step times the rate and the frame rate only sets how often a tick
comes. The heading counts frames of a cycle instead of seconds.

effects-feel: the pace is set a frame at a time, so one frame a second at ×1 is motion, not steps (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Rate ×1 moves each loop a quarter of a designed second a frame, whatever
the frame rate: a frame that steps the whole one-fps bar reads as a step,
a quarter of it as motion. The frame rate then sets how fast those frames
come. Rate keys still halve and double, ×1/8 to ×16.

effects-feel: keys for theme, frame rate and pace; starts over each cycle; frames painted whole (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

- SurfacePainter wraps every paint in DEC 2026 synchronized output, so a
  terminal that has it shows each frame whole: no row seen erased and not
  yet redrawn, which at 30 full-screen repaints a second read as flicker.
- App.rate is readable and settable; an animation goes on at the new rate
  from its next frame (tick() restarts the timer when the rate changes).
- The demo: n/p walk the bundled themes, </> step the frame rate, -/+ halve
  and double the demo's own pace, and the demo starts over after one cycle,
  the longest loop's period at that pace. Each loop's contrast is measured
  between the frames in 8 ms slices, so the first frame and a theme switch
  take ~50 ms instead of ~1.5 s.

effects-feel: --depth forces the depth it names; the run refuses any other (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

FORCE_COLOR was set to truecolor/256/ansi, values the library's detection
does not read, so every depth resolved to 16 colours while the heading said
truecolor. Now the chalk values 3/2/1, the table records the depth each
promises, runDemo throws if the console resolved another, and the test
asserts through detectColorSystem rather than pinning the strings.

effects-feel: breaths come in spells and rest after a sigh, wind gathers and slackens, halos never add (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Breath depth follows slow noise over the breaths, and the breath after a
sigh is quieter (x0.8) and late. Drift's advance surges between 0.33x and
1.15x STRIDE on noise over two periods. Overlapping firefly halos take
the brighter, as shimmer's passes do.

Worst 1 fps step over an hour: pulse 0.0395 (unchanged), drift
0.0286 -> 0.0256, sparkle 0.0324 -> 0.0236. A loose answering wave
between fireflies was tried and dropped: it bunched every turn's flashes
into one burst with long dark gaps.

effects-feel: a sigh catches once on the way in and draws in again (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

A swell is now a list of knots joined by raised cosines; breath and
firefly flash keep their shapes, and the sigh gains its double inhale.
Each part of the sigh's inhale climbs less steeply than a breath, so the
1 fps worst step over an hour stays 0.0395. REACH 0.3 -> 0.27 keeps a
whole-element rest between breaths now a sigh lasts 0.70 of its turn.
